stories.title: Men’s health awareness month highlights suicide rates
stories.summary: November is designated for raising awareness about men’s health, including mental health and suicide prevention. Keri Rudolph, CEO of The IV Bar Group, notes that South Africa records an average of 13,774 suicides annually. For many, the traditional expectation remains to endure pressure in silence.

stories.title: Experts identify youth behavioral health research priorities
stories.summary: A national consensus of sixty behavioral health experts has identified workforce development, cross-system financing, and peer support infrastructure as the most pressing research priorities for youth behavioral health. The initiative, led by the University of Connecticut, involved stakeholders from twenty-two states to address systemic service gaps.

stories.title: Psychologist warns of long-term impact from toxic bosses
stories.summary: Prolonged exposure to workplace criticism and intimidation can lead to emotional exhaustion, anxiety, and depression, according to Malaysian Psychological Association president Dr. Shazli Ezzat Ghazali. He warns that such relationships affect employee wellbeing long after they leave the office, undermining confidence and sleep patterns.

stories.title: Shipping container repurposed for mental health support
stories.summary: A shipping container in Orange Farm, South Africa, has been converted into a sensory room to provide mental health support. Originally designed for children with developmental conditions, the space now serves as a local resource for parents and caregivers where professional therapy is otherwise scarce.

stories.title: Commentary proposes triage framework for disaster preparedness
stories.summary: A study in BJPsych International identifies a structural gap between training and operational deployment in disaster preparedness. Authors propose a stepped-care psychological triage framework to help low- and middle-income countries mobilize trained personnel more effectively during emergencies, bridging the divide between individual competency and service delivery.

stories.title: YouTube faces $3 billion settlement over student addiction, mental health claims - IMPACT Magazine
Framework proposes proactive mental health screening for bereaved parents
stories.summary: A perspective paper in the Israel Journal of Health Policy Research argues for replacing patient-initiated help-seeking with proactive clinical screening for traumatically bereaved parents. The framework suggests that healthcare systems should assign institutional responsibility for mental health support rather than relying on parents to seek it out.

stories.title: Peer support linked to recovery through hope and inclusion
stories.summary: A multicentre randomized controlled trial found that structured peer support influences mental health recovery primarily by increasing hope and social inclusion. Researchers observed that while the interventions did not show statistically significant direct effects on clinical health, they fostered vital psychological resources for participants.

stories.title: Neighbors' Fight Kills Mental Health Worker At NJ Apartments For All To See: Report - DailyVoice.com
Virtual reality mindfulness pilot tests stress relief for hospital staff
stories.summary: A pilot study from Karolinska Institutet and Uppsala University found that a single virtual reality mindfulness session was perceived as relaxing by healthcare professionals. The researchers evaluated whether immersive digital tools could provide effective recovery breaks for staff facing high workplace pressure and workforce shortages.

stories.title: Parents’ homemade sensory room for children helps mental health problems - AP News
Kilgore High School students launch mental health support group
stories.summary: Students at Kilgore High School have established the Quiet Wellness Coalition, a student-led organization designed to provide mental health support to their peers. The group is part of a broader community landscape that includes life skills programs and local charitable meal distributions.

stories.title: Researchers develop AI app to identify emotional patterns
stories.summary: The Universidad Carlos III de Madrid and Psiconnea have developed the EMOTINET app, which uses AI to identify emotional patterns and recommend tailored content. The project aims to help users spot early signs of distress and strengthen emotional clarity as a knowledge-transfer initiative.

stories.title: Study finds two-week AI break reduces loneliness
stories.summary: A randomized experiment with 625 participants found that a 14-day pause from AI assistants resulted in a modest reduction in loneliness and increased in-person socializing. The findings, posted on arXiv, suggest that even brief changes in technology habits may influence human connection.

stories.title: ChatGPT usage linked to minor changes in loneliness
stories.summary: Researchers from Stanford, Oxford, and Carnegie Mellon found that users who stopped using ChatGPT for 14 days reported slightly less loneliness than those who stopped for one day. The effect was small and based on self-reported surveys, despite most participants using the tool primarily for work.

stories.title: Two-week break from AI assistants shows modest social benefits
stories.summary: A study of 625 US participants found that taking a two-week break from AI assistants led to a modest reduction in reported loneliness. Participants assigned the longer break also reported increased in-person contact compared to those who only stopped for one day.

stories.title: Breathwork study explores potential for altered states
stories.summary: Mental health professionals reported psychedelic-like shifts in consciousness during a study on rapid, continuous breathing. While participants noted potential for treating anxiety and depression, authors emphasized that firsthand enthusiasm does not establish the technique as a medical treatment and warned against use for severe psychiatric disorders.

stories.title: Report finds Americans increasingly acclimated to high stress
stories.summary: The American Psychological Association’s 2026 Stress in America report indicates that 74% of U.S. adults identify the future of the nation as a significant stressor. The report suggests that many adults are becoming accustomed to living with elevated stress as a background element of daily life.

stories.title: Irregular sleep schedules tied to heart risk
stories.summary: Researchers analyzing six months of Fitbit data from 10,000 American adults found that variable sleep duration and irregular bedtimes correlate with higher risks of heart and metabolic problems. The findings suggest that sleep regularity may be as important to cardiovascular health as the total number of hours slept.

stories.title: Young adults blame smartphones for poor sleep
stories.summary: A Pew Research Center study found 62 percent of Americans aged 18 to 29 believe smartphone use negatively affects their sleep. Overall, 41 percent of American adults reported that their devices hinder rest, while only 5 percent claimed the technology helped them sleep.

stories.title: Sleep disruption linked to memory fog
stories.summary: The brain uses sleep to review daily experiences, strengthen memories, and clear out waste. When sleep is disrupted, these maintenance processes are impaired, potentially leading to the mental fog and memory lapses often attributed to stress or tiredness.

stories.title: Chronic insomnia and intrusive thoughts
stories.summary: Clinicians treating patients with unwanted, harm-related thoughts report that these experiences are often familiar to those suffering from chronic insomnia. The distress frequently stems from patients questioning their own character because of thoughts they neither wanted nor chose.

stories.title: Daily movement suggested for better sleep
stories.summary: A study published in the Journal of Physical Activity and Health suggests that 10 minutes of daily movement, such as walking or taking breaks from sitting, supports healthier sleep architecture in young adults. The researchers note that exercise is not an overnight cure for insomnia.

stories.title: Long sleep duration linked to mortality in heart patients
stories.summary: A study of 3,287 adults with heart disease found that those sleeping nine or more hours per night faced a higher risk of death than those sleeping seven to eight hours. The data was drawn from the 2004 National Health Survey and tracked until 2019.

stories.title: IIT Madras opens new sleep study facility
stories.summary: Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava inaugurated a new sleep study facility and autism lab at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras on November 22. The campus health center will now offer specialized assessments as part of the institute's broader healthcare research and assistive technology initiatives.

stories.title: Vitamin D levels associated with sleep quality
stories.summary: A study of 460 individuals published in The Journal of Gerontology found that higher vitamin D levels are associated with longer total sleep times and fewer interruptions. Conversely, vitamin D deficiency was linked to shorter sleep durations in middle-aged and older adults.

stories.title: University of Pittsburgh Study Finds Daily Movement Matches Gym Exercise for Older Adults - Qoo Media
Somatic anxiety predicts karate match outcomes
stories.summary: A pilot study of elite female karate athletes found that self-reported somatic anxiety predicted match outcomes, while physiological markers like salivary cortisol and pro-inflammatory cytokines did not. Biomarker levels failed to distinguish winners from defeated peers during the national team selection tournament.

stories.title: Exercise may combat post-stroke depression
stories.summary: A study of over 1,000 patients published in the journal Stroke suggests that regular physical activity before and after a stroke can help combat resulting depression, anxiety, and exhaustion. Researchers noted that the specific impact of pre-stroke activity on these outcomes is not yet fully understood.

stories.title: Work-related physical activity linked to higher stress
stories.summary: A study of 15,688 residents in Japan found that physical activity performed for work can increase stress levels, unlike leisure-based exercise such as walking or sports. The research suggests that the context of movement matters for health outcomes.

Strength training recommended for weight-loss drug users
stories.summary: A clinical trial found that adults taking weight-loss medications lost nearly 50 pounds over 40 weeks regardless of exercise. Participants who added three weekly strength-training sessions preserved more lean tissue and maintained strength, while those who did not train experienced a decline in physical power.

stories.title: Cycling and brain training for cognitive impairment
stories.summary: A study of 146 older adults with mild cognitive impairment found that cycling combined with computer-based brain training preserved brain structures linked to Alzheimer’s disease. An independent expert noted the combination was not significantly more effective than cycling alone.

stories.title: Aerobic exercise and brain games for memory
stories.summary: A study published in JAMA Network Open suggests that aerobic exercise combined with brain-challenging activities may help preserve memory-related brain structures in older adults with mild cognitive impairment. Participants engaged in activities three times a week for six months, followed by an 18-month observation period.

stories.title: Core exercises suggested for knee osteoarthritis
stories.summary: A randomized controlled trial in India found that adding core-strengthening exercises to standard rehabilitation programs improved physical function for patients with knee osteoarthritis more than conventional therapy alone. The researchers suggest abdominal work may provide a trickle-down effect for knee stability.

stories.title: Polishing millets strips them of vital nutrients
stories.summary: Polishing millets removes the bran, aleurone layer and part of the germ, according to a study in the Indian Journal of Medical Research. While the process makes grains whiter, softer and longer-lasting, it leaves behind only the starchy endosperm. Nutrition is apparently an optional extra for shelf life.

stories.title: Four Demonized Foods That May Actually Offer Health Benefits - SSBCrack News
stories.summary: More than half of Americans say they obsess over food choices, from how much protein they consume to which ingredients they check and which foods they label “good” or “bad.” But some foods often treated as dietary villains may offer nutritional benefits when eaten as part of a balanced diet.

stories.title: Keto diet slashes liver fat in clinical trial
stories.summary: A study in Cell Metabolism found that participants on a ketogenic diet saw liver fat drop by 67 percent over four months. While all groups lost similar weight, half of the keto participants no longer met prediabetes criteria. The liver seems to have its own preferences.

stories.title: AARP says adults 50 and older are driving longevity market
stories.summary: AARP CEO Myechia Minter-Jordan says adults 50 and older are reshaping the health market and longevity conversations with physicians. The group produced 12.5 trillion dollars in economic activity in 2024. Longevity is now a significant line item in the national budget.

stories.title: Genetic study reveals secrets of 194-year-old tortoise
stories.summary: Researchers identified 287 genetic variants in Jonathan the giant tortoise associated with DNA repair, inflammation control and cancer suppression. The findings suggest his longevity involves both inherited traits and the preservation of cellular functions. Evolution has clearly spent more time on him than on us.

stories.title: Social engagement linked to longevity in 90+ study
stories.summary: Dr. Claudia Kawas of UC Irvine has tracked residents in their 90s for decades to identify factors associated with long life. While diet and exercise are common focuses, everyday social engagement stood out as a primary habit. The secret to living longer may simply be talking to people.

stories.summary: They're sixty-three, in a beginner ceramics class, and their bowl looks like something a child abandoned halfway through. Their hands won't do what their minds are picturing. The walls are uneven. There's a crack in the bottom. The person next to them, who is also sixty-three, is somehow already on

stories.title: How much exercise is needed to maintain good health in old age?
stories.summary: (Dan Tri Newspaper) - Even if you don't reach the recommended level of exercise, short periods of physical activity each day can still benefit your health, especially for those who are less active. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends that adults engage in at least 150-300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic

stories.title: VO2 Max in Your 70s May Predict Your Brain Health a Decade Later
stories.summary: VO2 max has been linked to everything from cardiovascular disease risk to metabolic health, cognitive performance, and even overall mortality. It shows up in research on longevity as one of the powerful markers reflecting how well your body is functioning under stress. And now, a new long-term study1 builds on

stories.title: MIND diet fails to cut death risk in 20-year study
stories.summary: A 20-year study of 15,000 adults found the MIND diet was not linked to a longer life once social factors were accounted for. The diet, designed to protect the aging brain, showed only a small link to one measure of thinking skills. Results may vary by bank account.

stories.title: Nepal and India exchange MoU for traditional medicine cooperation
stories.summary: Nepal and India will exchange a Memorandum of Understanding to expand bilateral cooperation in Ayurveda and traditional medicine systems. The agreement aims to support conservation efforts, scientific research, and technical exchange between the two nations. The formal signing is scheduled between officials from both governments.

Acupuncture research for cancer nausea faces evidence gaps
stories.summary: A scoping review of hundreds of clinical investigations found that methodological shortcomings and structural evidence gaps hinder consistent clinical practice recommendations for acupuncture and moxibustion in cancer care. While these interventions are widely studied, international panels continue to maintain conflicting stances on their use for nausea and vomiting.

stories.title: Acupuncture shows benefit for persistent fatigue in breast cancer
stories.summary: The AcuBreast trial suggests that individualized acupuncture integrated with routine care provides clinically meaningful relief for breast cancer survivors experiencing fatigue lasting six months or more. The study evaluated the intervention under real-world conditions, demonstrating symptom reductions across multiple validated outcome measures for patients.

stories.title: Somatic therapy gains popularity alongside safety concerns
stories.summary: Somatic therapy has become a social media buzzword, leading to questions regarding practitioner training and accountability. While proponents highlight the potential for unlocking emotions held in the body, experts suggest that individuals should proceed with caution to ensure a trauma-informed environment is present during sessions.

stories.title: Ayurveda hospital provides relief to Sabarimala pilgrims
stories.summary: The Kerala government has established an Ayurveda hospital at Sabarimala to treat pilgrims suffering from sprains and joint pain following the trek to the hill shrine. The facility employs 21 staff members, including seven doctors, to provide herbal treatments and massages to visiting devotees.

stories.title: NASA rover finds unusual rock formations on Mars
stories.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover has identified disk-shaped, crystal-like structures embedded in Martian bedrock at a site nicknamed Nazca. The formations feature warped, curled edges that resemble potato chips. Researchers are currently investigating the composition and origin of these structures found during a recent drilling operation.

stories.title: Massage therapy expands into canine wellness
stories.summary: Canine massage therapy is gaining traction as owners seek to apply human health care practices to their pets. Practitioners focus on maintenance for senior dogs, specifically targeting hip and lower back issues. The field remains in a developing stage as more specialized services enter the market.

stories.title: Sat Kartar Life plans Bengaluru Ayurveda hospital
stories.summary: Sat Kartar Life Limited proposes a 1.25 crore rupee investment for a 10-bed Ayurveda hospital in Bengaluru. The 6,500 square foot facility expects to begin therapy services in December 2026, with full operations targeted for March 2027, pending necessary regulatory approvals.
